title_en: Agricultural Bank of China, Harbin Taiping Sub-branch v. Harbin Songhuajiang Dairy Cattle Co., Ltd., Harbin Gongda Group Co., Ltd., and Harbin Zhonglong Accounting Firm Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan contract
ruling_gist_en: 1. Although the act of a debtor signing or affixing its seal on a notice of overdue debt demand issued by a creditor does not necessarily indicate that the debtor is willing to perform the obligation, it may indicate that the debtor acknowledges the existence of the debt, which constitutes an admission by the party of the civil debt relationship. The people's court may find accordingly that a debt relationship exists between the parties.
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over loan contract; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Heilongjiang Province; Legal person; Financial institution; Civil Procedure Law; Effect of overdue debt demand notice; Assumption of debts after restructuring of state-owned enterprises; Waiver of right to appeal and scope of appellate review; Affirm the original judgment; Loan contract; Maximum amount mortgage; Restructuring of state-owned enterprises; Debt collection; Good faith; Contract dispute; Loan contract dispute of a limited company
full_text_en:
Agricultural Bank of China, Harbin Taiping Sub-branch v. Harbin Songhuajiang Dairy Co., Ltd., Harbin Gongda Group Co., Ltd., and Harbin Zhonglong Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Loan Contract

【Ruling Summary】

1. The act of a debtor signing or affixing its seal on a debt overdue reminder notice issued by a creditor, while not necessarily indicating the debtor's willingness to perform the debt, may indicate its acknowledgment of the existence of such debt. This constitutes a self-admission by the party concerning the civil debt relationship. The people's court may determine that a debt relationship exists between the parties based on this.

2. After the restructuring of a state-owned enterprise, the original debts shall be assumed by the restructured enterprise. If a creditor issues a debt overdue reminder notice to the restructured enterprise, it shall be deemed as the creditor's recognition of the change in the debtor.

3. The right to appeal is a procedural right granted to a party by law, which the party may exercise or waive. According to Article 151 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, when a people's court of second instance hears an appeal case, it shall review the issues related to the facts and application of law raised in the appellant's appeal. If a party fails to file an appeal within the statutory period but raises objections to the first-instance judgment during the second-instance proceedings, the people's court of second instance shall not review such objections.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2007) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 178

Appellant (Original Defendant): Harbin Songhuajiang Dairy Co., Ltd., domiciled at Changsheng Village, Dongfeng Town, Taiping District, Harbin, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal Representative: Dong Ping, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Yuen, Lawyer, Heilongjiang Guangyuan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Kaibo, Legal Counsel, Harbin Gongda Group Co., Ltd.

Respondent (Original Plaintiff): Agricultural Bank of China, Harbin Taiping Sub-branch, domiciled at No. 446 Dongzhi Road, Daowai District, Harbin.

Responsible Person: Wang Xiaoming, Deputy Manager of the Sub-branch.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Huidong, Lawyer, Heilongjiang Yinlong Law Firm.

Original Defendant: Harbin Gongda Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 118 Xidazhi Street, Nangang District, Harbin, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Dacheng, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Xuedong, Head of the Legal Department of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Kaibo, Legal Counsel of the Company.

Original Defendant: Harbin Zhonglong Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 5 Zhongxuan Street, Nangang District, Harbin, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal Representative: Zhao Zhijie, Chairman of the Board.

The appellant, Harbin Songhuajiang Dairy Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Dairy Company), filed an appeal with this Court against the Civil Judgment (2006) Hei Gao Shang Chu Zi No. 20 of the Higher People's Court of Heilongjiang Province in the dispute over a loan contract involving the respondent, Agricultural Bank of China, Harbin Taiping Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Taiping Agricultural Bank), and the original defendants, Harbin Gongda Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Gongda Group) and Harbin Zhonglong Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhonglong Accounting Firm). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Qian Xiaochen serving as the Presiding Judge, and Acting Judges Liu Min and Yang Zhengyu as members, to hear the case. Court Clerk Yuan Hongxia served as the recorder. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts: On March 3, 1998, Harbin Songhuajiang Dairy Farm (hereinafter referred to as the Dairy Farm) and Taiping Agricultural Bank signed a "Maximum Amount Mortgage Guarantee Loan Contract" for a loan amount of RMB 19 million, with a loan term from March 3, 1998 to February 28, 1999, an interest rate of 7.92 per mille, and overdue interest calculated at a daily rate of 0.4 per mille. The Dairy Farm provided its own office building, vehicles, and cow sheds as mortgage collateral, but the mortgage was not registered. Taiping Agricultural Bank disbursed the loan as contracted. Upon the maturity of the loan, the Dairy Farm failed to perform its repayment obligation. In February 2001, the Economic and Trade Commission of Heilongjiang Province established Heilongjiang Dairy Group Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Black Dairy Group), and the Dairy Farm became subordinate to it. In 2003, the Heilongjiang Provincial Government restructured the assets of Black Dairy Group. Heilongjiang Provincial Investment Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Provincial Investment) commissioned Heilongjiang Zhongrui Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongrui Company) to appraise the assets of Black Dairy Group, including the Dairy Farm. The net assets of the Dairy Farm were valued at RMB 91,242,800. The effective period for this appraisal conclusion was from June 30, 2003 to June 29, 2004. On September 22, 2003, Gongda Group acquired Black Dairy Group for a consideration of RMB 79 million. In May 2004, Gongda Group contributed the net assets of the Dairy Farm, valued at RMB 47.5 million, as capital to establish the Dairy Company jointly with Harbin Tongcheng Investment Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tongcheng Company). On July 12, 2004, based on the appraisal report of Zhongrui Company, Zhonglong Accounting Firm issued a capital verification report, confirming that Gongda Group's capital contribution was genuine. In December 2004, Taiping Agricultural Bank issued a "Debt Overdue Reminder Notice" to the Dairy Company, demanding repayment of the principal of RMB 35.15 million (including the RMB 19 million in question) and interest. In June 2006, Taiping Agricultural Bank again issued a "Debt Overdue Reminder Notice" to the Dairy Company for the principal of RMB 35.15 million, with the interest column crossed out. The Dairy Company affixed its seal on both reminder notices as confirmation.

It was also found that on July 14, 2004, the Dairy Farm was restructured and changed its name to the Dairy Company, with changes in enterprise type, business scope, and registered capital registered with the Daowai Branch of the Harbin Administration for Industry and Commerce.

On April 28, 2006, Taiping Agricultural Bank filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, alleging that: Upon the maturity of the loan period, the Dairy Farm failed to repay the overdue debt; Gongda Group, as the purchaser of the Dairy Farm, should bear civil liability with all its property, including its equity in the Dairy Company; Zhonglong Accounting Firm, as the capital verification institution for shareholder capital contributions, had issued a false capital verification report and should bear joint and several compensation liability to Taiping Agricultural Bank to the extent of the false amount verified. The plaintiff requested a judgment ordering the Dairy Company, Gongda Group, and Zhonglong Accounting Firm to jointly repay the outstanding loan of RMB 19 million; interest of RMB 12,208,529 accrued up to March 20, 2006; overdue interest of RMB 4,624,847.37; attorney fees of RMB 1.075 million; and litigation costs.

After trial, the court of first instance held that: The loan portion of the "Maximum Amount Mortgage Guarantee Loan Contract" signed between Taiping Agricultural Bank and the Dairy Farm represented the true intent of both parties and did not violate prohibitive provisions of laws and regulations, and thus should be deemed legally valid and effective. The mortgage guarantee portion did not come into legal effect due to the failure to register the mortgaged property. According to the loan contract signed by both parties, Taiping Agricultural Bank performed its obligation to disburse the loan as agreed. Upon the maturity of the loan, the Dairy Farm failed to repay it and should bear liability for breach of contract. After the Dairy Farm was restructured into the Dairy Company, although its property rights structure, organizational form, and name changed, its creditor-debtor relationship persisted. The restructured Dairy Company was essentially a continuation of the original Dairy Farm. Therefore, the Dairy Company should be the entity responsible for assuming the debt.

Regarding the amount of the loan and interest. On March 3, 1998, the Dairy Farm borrowed RMB 19 million from Taiping Agricultural Bank and signed and affixed its seal on the loan receipt at the borrower's place. The Dairy Company did not deny the authenticity of its seal. The eight loan receipts presented by the Dairy Company, totaling RMB 16.15 million, did not match the loan amount or time of the loan contract in this case. The Dairy Company admitted to having a cumulative outstanding loan principal of RMB 35.15 million with Taiping Agricultural Bank. The eight loan receipts presented by the Dairy Company should pertain to another eight separate loans unrelated to the RMB 19 million in this lawsuit. Moreover, the loan contract in this lawsuit was consistent with the loan receipt in terms of amount and time. Therefore, the Dairy Company's claim that the loan amount was RMB 16.15 million and that Taiping Agricultural Bank did not fully perform its contractual obligations lacked factual basis and was not supported by the court. Regarding the Dairy Company's argument, based on the crossed-out interest column in the June 2006 "Debt Overdue Reminder Notice," that Taiping Agricultural Bank had waived its claim for interest, since the Dairy Company failed to present evidence of an agreement with Taiping Agricultural Bank on interest exemption, the fact that Taiping Agricultural Bank crossed out the interest column only indicated that it did not claim a specific amount of interest, and it could not lead to the conclusion of interest exemption. Statutory fruits on bank loans cannot be exempted. Therefore, the court did not support the Dairy Company's claim for interest exemption. The amount of interest should be calculated in accordance with the loan contract and the standard interest rates for current loans and overdue loans of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding periods.

Regarding the issues of false capital contribution by Gongda Group and false capital verification by Zhonglong Accounting Firm, and their liability. In 2003, the provincial government restructured the assets of Black Dairy Group. Provincial Investment commissioned Zhongrui Company to appraise the assets of the Dairy Farm and publicly invited bids based on the appraised value. Through bidding, Gongda Group acquired ownership of Black Dairy Group for a consideration of RMB 79 million. Gongda Group used the appraised net assets of the Dairy Farm as its capital contribution. Zhonglong Accounting Firm issued a capital verification report based on an appraisal conclusion that had expired by 12 days. Although this was a defect, Taiping Agricultural Bank did not present evidence that the capital verification report contained false records, misleading statements, or material omissions. According to Article 2, Paragraph 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Trial of Cases Involving Civil Tort Compensation for Accounting Firms in Audit Business Activities," this alone cannot prove that Gongda Group made a false capital contribution or that Zhonglong Accounting Firm made a false capital verification. Furthermore, Taiping Agricultural Bank did not suffer losses due to reliance on or use of this capital verification report. Therefore, the court did not support Taiping Agricultural Bank's claim for Zhonglong Accounting Firm to bear liability. In September 2003, Gongda Group acquired all of Black Dairy Group, including the Dairy Farm. The assets of the original Dairy Farm were transferred to Gongda Group. In the "Overall Property Transfer Contract," Gongda Group undertook to "assume all debts of the acquired enterprise and ensure the proper resolution of debt relationships between the acquired enterprise and creditor banks." Therefore, Gongda Group should perform its contractual obligations and bear liability for repayment when the Dairy Company is unable to satisfy its debts. On March 3, 1998, Taiping Agricultural Bank disbursed the loan, with the performance period ending on February 28, 1999. In December 2004, Taiping Agricultural Bank demanded repayment of this loan from the Dairy Company. Although the statute of limitations had already expired, the Dairy Company confirmed by affixing its seal on the "Debt Overdue Reminder Notice," which was deemed as reaching a new debt repayment agreement between the parties, and the statute of limitations ran anew. By the time Taiping Agricultural Bank filed the lawsuit in June 2006, the statute of limitations had not expired. The court did not support Gongda Group's defense that the statute of limitations had expired. Regarding Taiping Agricultural Bank's claim for attorney fees, as there was no such agreement between the parties and Taiping Agricultural Bank did not provide other evidence to support it, the court did not support this claim.

In summary, Taiping Agricultural Bank's claims were partially reasonable and were supported by the court of first instance. In accordance with Articles 206 and 207 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the court of first instance ruled: 1. The defendant Dairy Company shall pay the plaintiff Taiping Agricultural Bank RMB 19 million in principal and interest (interest calculated according to the loan contract and the current and overdue loan interest rates of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding periods) within ten days from the effective date of this judgment. 2. If the defendant Dairy Company fails to satisfy the above debts, the defendant Gongda Group shall be responsible for their satisfaction. 3. All other claims of the plaintiff Taiping Agricultural Bank are dismissed. If the obligation to pay money is not performed within the period specified in the judgment, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The case acceptance fee of RMB 160,010 shall be borne by the Dairy Company and Gongda Group.

The Dairy Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, filed an appeal with this Court, arguing: 1. According to Article 29 of the "General Rules on Loans" issued by the People's Bank of China in 1996: "All loans shall be accompanied by a loan contract signed by the lender and the borrower." The court of first instance's finding that the appellant Dairy Company owed the respondent Taiping Agricultural Bank a loan of RMB 19 million lacked a contractual basis. Similarly, the respondent Taiping Agricultural Bank's claim for repayment of the debt against the appellant Dairy Company lacked a contractual basis. 2. The "Maximum Amount Mortgage Guarantee Loan Contract" submitted by the respondent Taiping Agricultural Bank to the court of first instance should be an invalid contract. The formation of this contract was predicated on the existence of a loan contract. Its main content stipulated that if the borrower failed to perform its repayment obligation upon maturity under the loan contract, the borrower would use the collateral to repay the loan. However, the mortgage guarantee contract involved in this case not only lacked a principal contract (i.e., a loan contract) as its basis, but its agreed content was also not performed in practice. The first item of the mortgage guarantee contract stated that the appellant would guarantee the performance of the RMB 19 million contract with its office building, vehicles, cow sheds, etc. Because the parties did not complete the relevant mortgage formalities, the mortgage act was invalid, and the mortgage contract was void. 3. Although the appellant Dairy Company issued a loan receipt for RMB 19 million to the respondent, this amount was not credited to the appellant Dairy Company's account. The appellant Dairy Company did not use the loan to purchase feed as stated in the loan receipt. According to the legal principle of consistency of rights and obligations under Chinese law, since the appellant Dairy Company did not use the loan as agreed, it had no obligation to repay the loan and interest. 4. The appellant Dairy Company is a legal entity and should independently bear civil liability. Gongda Group's acquisition in 2003 did not affect the appellant's civil capacity for rights and conduct, i.e., its status as a civil entity. The RMB 19 million loan claimed by the respondent occurred in 1998, five years before the acquisition, and is unrelated to Gongda Group. Therefore, Gongda Group should not bear liability for its satisfaction.

During the second-instance proceedings, the Dairy Company submitted the following new evidence: 1. A bank statement for March 1998 for account number 075300873000843 issued by Dongfeng Sub-branch to the Dairy Farm, purporting to prove that the RMB 19 million loan under the "Maximum Amount Mortgage Guarantee Loan Contract" signed between the Dairy Farm and Taiping Agricultural Bank was not actually performed. The statement shows that on March 6, 1998, under account 075300873000843, there was a "credit" of RMB 19 million and a "debit" of RMB 19 million on the same day. This means that a sum of RMB 19 million entered and exited the Dairy Farm's account at the Agricultural Bank Dongfeng Sub-branch on March 6, 1998. 2. The Dairy Farm's "Bank Deposit Journal" purporting to show that the RMB 19 million loan did not enter the Dairy Farm's account. 3. A bank statement for March 1999 between the Dairy Farm and Dongfeng Sub-branch. This evidence shows that funds were transferred into the Dairy Farm's account and then withdrawn on the same day, purportedly to prove that Taiping Agricultural Bank frequently engaged in improper practices, such as same-day entry and exit, or "empty loans," to boost performance. To support this evidence, the appellant also submitted 10 bank loan repayment vouchers between the Dairy Farm and Taiping Agricultural Bank for March 1999. Based on the above, the Dairy Company requested that the court of second instance set aside the original judgment and order the respondent to bear all litigation costs in this case.

The Respondent Taiping Agricultural Bank argued in its defense: Taiping Agricultural Bank's claim for repayment of principal and interest from the Dairy Company has a contractual basis. The court of first instance correctly found that a loan contract relationship existed between the two, which is supported by facts. The second and third grounds of appeal in the appellant's petition are baseless appeals and are not relevant to the appeal request. Regarding the "Maximum Amount Mortgage Guarantee Loan Contract" signed by the parties in this case, the court of first instance correctly found that the mortgage guarantee portion did not take effect due to the failure to register the mortgaged property. The second ground of appeal targets a non-existent issue and constitutes a baseless appeal. The third ground of appeal attempts to sever the historical connection between the Dairy Company and the Dairy Farm before its restructuring and name change, which is both factually and legally untenable. The appellant has no standing to raise grounds of appeal on behalf of the original defendant Gongda Group, and the court of second instance should not hear them. As for the bank statements submitted by the Dairy Company during the second-instance proceedings, they bear no seal or stamp from the Agricultural Bank, and their authenticity cannot be confirmed. The Dairy Farm's "Bank Deposit Journal" was prepared unilaterally and has no evidentiary value. Furthermore, Taiping Agricultural Bank submitted a debit voucher "Agricultural Bank of China Loan Receipt" dated December 9, 1997, showing that on December 8, 1997, the Dairy Farm borrowed RMB 19 million from Taiping Agricultural Bank. This proves that the RMB 19 million principal claimed in this lawsuit originated from a "rolling over" of an existing overdue loan from 1997, i.e., an industry practice of "repaying the old by borrowing the new," and that the RMB 19 million was indeed actually used by the Dairy Farm. In summary, the facts found in the original judgment are clear, and the respondent requests the court of second instance to uphold the original judgment.

The Original Defendant Gongda Group stated during the second-instance proceedings of this Court that Taiping Agricultural Bank's request for Gongda Group to bear repayment liability has exceeded the statute of limitations, and Gongda Group should not bear repayment liability.

This Court confirms the facts found in the original judgment.

This Court holds: Based on the parties' appeal and defense arguments, the issues in dispute in this second-instance trial focus on three aspects: First, whether the debt of RMB 19 million actually arose between the Dairy Farm and Taiping Agricultural Bank; Second, if it did actually arise, whether the Dairy Company should assume this debt of the Dairy Farm; Third, whether the grounds and requests raised by the appellant regarding Gongda Group's non-liability fall within the scope of review in the second-instance proceedings.

I. The issue of whether the RMB 19 million debt actually arose between the Dairy Farm and Taiping Agricultural Bank.

First, we affirm the first-instance judgment's finding that the loan portion of the "Maximum Amount Mortgage Guarantee Loan Contract" signed between the Dairy Farm and Taiping Agricultural Bank in March 1998 was valid and legally effective, while the mortgage guarantee portion had not taken legal effect. We do not uphold the appellant Dairy Cattle Company's claim that the "Maximum Amount Mortgage Guarantee Loan Contract" signed between the Dairy Farm and Taiping Agricultural Bank was a void contract. Regarding the appellant's contention that the loan of RMB 19 million was not actually credited to the Dairy Farm's account, and that the Dairy Farm did not use the loan as agreed, and therefore had no obligation to repay the loan or pay interest, during the second instance of this case, the appellant submitted the March 1998 account statement from the Agricultural Bank Dongfeng Sub-branch and the Dairy Farm's "Bank Deposit Journal" showing that Taiping Agricultural Bank deducted the loan immediately after disbursement. This fact arose from outstanding debts between Taiping Agricultural Bank and the Dairy Farm. Due to the long-standing lending relationship between Taiping Agricultural Bank and the Dairy Farm, where disbursement and immediate deduction occurred multiple times, the possibility of using new loans to repay old loans cannot be excluded. In addition to the factual evidence of loan disbursement and deduction, the parties' admissions are also important evidence proving this relationship. The Dairy Cattle Company had previously, on December 17, 2004, affixed its official seal and had its legal representative sign and seal on Taiping Agricultural Bank's "Notice of Urging Overdue Debt Repayment" for a principal of RMB 35.15 million and interest of RMB 15,127,783.41; and on June 13, 2006, it again affixed its seal on Taiping Agricultural Bank's "Notice of Urging Overdue Debt Repayment" urging repayment of the principal of RMB 35.15 million. Although a debtor's act of signing or sealing on a payment reminder does not necessarily indicate its willingness to perform the original obligation, it can show that it acknowledges the existence of the original obligation and confirms receipt of the payment reminder. Furthermore, the two accounting statements provided by Zhonglong Accounting Firm show that the short-term borrowing item on the balance sheet is RMB 35.66 million, which is also consistent with the total amount of loans Taiping Agricultural Bank claims the Dairy Farm owes it. Moreover, the probative force of this evidence is superior to the "Bank Deposit Journal" submitted by the appellant. Therefore, based on the loan portion of the "Maximum Amount Mortgage Guarantee Loan Contract" signed between the Dairy Farm and Taiping Agricultural Bank on March 3, 1998; the fact that the Dairy Farm signed and sealed the loan receipt for the RMB 19 million loan on March 3, 1998; and the fact that the Dairy Cattle Company signed and sealed the "Notices of Urging Overdue Debt Repayment," we find that the creditor-debtor relationship of RMB 19 million between Taiping Agricultural Bank and the Dairy Farm exists.

II. Whether the Dairy Cattle Company shall assume this debt of the Dairy Farm.

In May 2004, Gongda Group contributed the Dairy Farm's net assets to co-establish the Dairy Cattle Company with Tongcheng Company. This constitutes a change in the corporate form of a state-owned enterprise, i.e., a state-owned enterprise incorporating new shares to form a limited liability company. After the enterprise's restructuring, its rights and obligations shall be assumed by the changed enterprise. At the second instance hearing of this case, the Dairy Cattle Company acknowledged that it would assume the debts of the Dairy Farm. The act of Taiping Agricultural Bank issuing a notice of debt collection to the Dairy Cattle Company also indicates that Taiping Agricultural Bank, as the creditor, approved this change of debtor. Therefore, there is no dispute between the parties that the Dairy Cattle Company assumes this debt of the Dairy Farm, and we affirm this.

III. Whether the reasons and requests raised by the appellant that Gongda Group should not bear liability fall within the scope of second-instance review.

The second-instance procedure commences upon a party's appeal. The right to appeal is a litigation right granted to parties by law, which a party may either exercise or waive. If a party does not appeal after the first-instance judgment, it indicates that the party accepts the first-instance people's court's handling of their civil rights and obligations. In this case, Gongda Group, as the defendant at first instance, did not appeal to this court within the statutory period. It merely stated in its agent ad litem's submissions to the collegial panel that Gongda Group should not bear the liability for payment when the Dairy Cattle Company is unable to pay its debts to Taiping Agricultural Bank. Pursuant to Article 151 of the Civil Procedure Law, the second-instance people's court, when hearing an appealed case, shall review the relevant facts and the application of law concerning the issues appealed by the parties. Therefore, the requests raised by Gongda Group shall not be reviewed in the second instance. Regarding the claim made by the Dairy Cattle Company in its appeal petition that Gongda Group should not bear liability, since Gongda Group is an independent enterprise legal person, the Dairy Cattle Company has no right to raise an appeal request on whether Gongda Group bears liability. Consequently, the request of the Dairy Cattle Company that Gongda Group should not bear liability is not subject to this court's review.

In conclusion, the first-instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court hereby adjudicates as follows:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The court acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 135,800, to be borne by Harbin Songhua River Dairy Cattle Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Qian Xiaochen

Acting Judge: Liu Min
